content.thinking:
I'm going through the overview claims one by one. So far each checks out against the summary: the outage duration, the peak error rate, and the cause, a setting that routed account pages through new monthly-spending code. I'm now on the fifth claim, the estimate of what the shop lost.

I'm checking the remaining claims against the record. The customer loss estimate is backed by the assumptions, and the claim that nobody was paged holds up against the figures. The rollback of the feature flag is confirmed and still in place. The proposed code fix, PR #581, is only a draft, so I'm noting that it hasn't been applied. Nothing in these needs flagging.

supported.quote: For {duration}, some shoppers on io-shop could not load their account pages.
rows: What a reader saw: Shoppers' account pages failed
Summary: The service broke at 12:21 UTC and was back to normal at 12:29 UTC

supported.quote: At the worst minute, {peak_error_rate} of requests were failing.
rows: Requests failing at the worst minute: 40.5% {peak_error_rate}

supported.quote: Someone had switched on a setting that sent account pages through new monthly-spending code.
That code likely breaks for shoppers who have bought before but not this month, so their account pages failed.
Argus estimates the shop lost {customer_loss} in takings.
rows: What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): 5,194.52 USD {customer_loss}

supported.quote: Nobody was paged, so no on-call responders were called out.
rows: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

supported.quote: To end the incident, Argus turned the setting back off by reverting the feature flag monthly-spend-feature. That change is confirmed and still in place.
rows: Argus: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature - confirmed, still in place

supported.quote: Argus has also proposed a fix to the code as PR #581, but it is still a draft and has not been applied.
rows: Argus: proposed a fix, PR #581 - opened as a draft
Supporting information: The fix it proposed: PR #581 ... opened as a draft. The record holds nothing about it after that.
